claim_being_audited: Whether rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-042 as a procurement-risk decision is compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk at the time of decision.
specific_concerns: The policy requires admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk for rejection, but the record here more clearly supports follow-up or escalation than a reject-level finding.
BPROC-042-D explicitly says no failed control test is logged, which weakens any implication that a control failure was established.
BPROC-042-C and BPROC-042-D show process gaps and inconsistency, but the policy text states those items do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
BPROC-042-E recommends follow-up before approval if storage controls remain unresolved; it does not itself recommend rejection.
The actor's framing of an 'unresolved control posture' is plausible, but the packet overstates how strongly the admissible record supports rejection rather than further diligence.
unsupported_claims: The record does not firmly establish that the questionnaire inconsistency was material enough, by itself or cumulatively, to satisfy the policy threshold for rejection.
The record does not show a documented reviewed control-binder requirement that was formally failed by the vendor.
The record does not show that approval readiness was formally denied under a logged procurement standard rather than left pending follow-up.
evidence_requests: A logged materiality determination explaining why the documented quality-process gap and storage inconsistency rose to reject-level risk.
Any admissible record showing the storage-control inconsistency remained unresolved at the decision time after follow-up was attempted or declined.
Any formal procurement or security review note concluding the vendor was not approvable, rather than merely requiring escalation or clarification.
Any admissible threshold or rubric showing that the cited delivery issue and documentation gap jointly satisfy rejection criteria.
decision_criteria: Reject only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Do not treat quality-process gaps or questionnaire inconsistencies alone as proof of a reject-level control failure.
Do not rely on unlogged or private security-review results.
Assess whether the cited evidence supports rejection itself, or only follow-up/escalation before an approval decision.
